say.en: A method is a named block of code that does one job. Write isPrime once and call it a hundred times, from anywhere in the class. In this lesson: Define and call methods with parameters and return values.

body.en: A method has a header and a body: access-specifier return-type name(parameter list) { body }. For example, int square(int x) { return x * x; }. The values passed in a call (actual parameters, or arguments) are copied into the formal parameters of the header. return sends a value back and ends the method; a void method returns nothing. The method signature is its name together with the number, types and order of its parameters.

points.en: Header: access, return type, name, parameters
return ends the method and sends a value
Actual parameters are copied into formal parameters

body.en: Two or more methods of a class may share a name if their parameter lists differ in number, type or order of parameters. This is *overloading*, a form of compile-time (static) polymorphism: the compiler picks the method whose parameters best match the call. The return type alone cannot distinguish overloaded methods. Example: int area(int s), double area(double r), int area(int l, int b).
